title: Unlock prefetch fairness to stop long-tail drowning in multi-tenant clusters
creator: Mei Chen
description: Multiple customers (hosted and private clusters) reported sudden spikes in short-request latency coinciding with bursts of long-context generations. Root cause analysis indicates a prefetch + admission budgeting interaction: the prefetch layer eagerly materializes KV cache slices for long-context requests which inflates the admission token consumption and then allows the scheduler to form a few very large batches. During these bursts, small latency-sensitive requests are deferred for multiple admission cycles, producing customer-visible queue starvation and long-context tail latency regressions. This ticket tracks the investigation, proposed fixes, and rollout for a mitigation that balances prefetch behavior against admission fairness across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Mei Chen: Ticket opened after PagerDuty escalation from two enterprise customers. Collected traces and p95/p99 latency from Console; initial hypothesis: prefetch-induced admission budget amplification.

2026-03-02 - Diego Alvarez: Reproduced locally with synthetic mix: 60% short (<32 tokens) QPS, 40% long (>=2048 tokens) sampled at bursts. Observed admission token drain pattern and KV prefetch wheel-up. Captured heap and kernel utilization during bursts.

2026-03-03 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented a low-risk experiment (runtime flag) to cap per-req prefetch tokens to 512 for long-contexts. Local perf: small-request median latency improved 2.8x under burst; long-request throughput degraded by <6%.

2026-03-04 - PM review (Evelyn Park): Confirmed customer impact matrix and prioritized P0. Agreed on canary plan: host a rollout on a single dedicated pool and one hosted region, plus staged Private customer patch.
2026-03-05 - Design/DEX (Arjun Patel): Suggested dashboard augmentations — admission token heatmap and per-tenant prefetch counters to surface regressions during canary.

2026-03-06 - Diego Alvarez: Opened GH PR #11874 with the prefetch cap + adaptive backoff prototype and unit tests. Note: PR toggles via config flag: scheduler.prefetch_budget_cap and scheduler.prefetch_backoff_factor.
2026-03-07 - QA (Nina Ramos): Ran regression suites on Dedicated simulator. Two flakes observed related to eviction timing; created a follow-up subtask ENG-102937 to harden eviction ordering.

2026-03-08 - Ops (Lucas Green): Deployed canary to hosted-us-west-2 and dedicated-pool-7 with the flag enabled at 10% traffic. Early telemetry: p50 small-request latency improved 18ms -> 9ms; p99 reduced by ~25%.
2026-03-09 - Customer success (Priya Nair): Engaged with reporting customers. One customer confirmed lower error spike incidents; another requested a private-patch timeline for on-prem.

2026-03-10 - Diego Alvarez: Preparing rollout runbook and automated rollback steps. Need final approval for merge after security review signoff; also scheduling deterministic replay canary (ENG-70233) to ensure no regression under mixed synthetic traces.
implementation_notes: Planned fix has three parts: 1) Introduce scheduler.prefetch_budget_cap (default 512 tokens) to limit per-request prefetch allocation for >1024-context models. 2) Add adaptive backoff: when admission queue detects >30% of recent batches dominated by long-context token count, progressively reduce prefetch cap by backoff factor per second up to 0.25x. 3) Expose per-tenant prefetch counters and admission token budgeting metrics in Console. The feature will be behind a runtime flag for safe rollout.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for budget math and backoff decay. 2) Integration in CI with mixed-length trace corpus (short/long rushes). 3) Dedicated cluster smoke tests on replica types (A100, H100) and Private on customer VM images. 4) Canary with deterministic replay (ENG-70233) for 48h at 10% traffic then 50% if stable.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag after security review. 2) Deploy to staging and run synthetic replay. 3) Canary on hosted-us-west-2 + dedicated-pool-7 + one Private customer image (coordinated with CSM). 4) Monitor admission heatmap and token saturation alarms for 72h. 5) Gradual ramp to 100% with 1-hour holds at 10/25/50/75/100.
rollback_plan: Toggle runtime flag off to restore previous prefetch behavior; if downstream eviction ordering regressions appear, revert the merge and re-enable previous canary. Keep snapshots of admission queue states to assist debugging.
risks: 1) Overly aggressive prefetch cap could reduce long-request throughput and increase cost. 2) Backoff oscillation risk under rapidly changing mix without hysteresis. 3) Private deployments with older runtime images may not support flag; patch coordination required.
open_questions: What default cap is acceptable across customers with very long contexts (>64k tokens)? (suggested follow-up: add model-specific caps)
Should we automatically tune backoff thresholds per-tenant based on historical mix or keep global defaults?
Do we require a formal security review for exposing per-tenant prefetch counters in Console?
